paras: The stoning of Preston Bland occurred on the night of Saturday, August 1, 1903, when a crowd on Manhattan's West Side threw stones at Bland, a Black longshoreman, as four policemen took him to the West Sixty-eighth street station after a shooting. Bland, accused of wounding a white passer-by, was held in $1,000 bail; the crowd episode is known only from a policeman's testimony as reported by the New York Sun.

According to Policeman Gerhard, Bland quarrelled with another Black man near Sixty-fourth street and Amsterdam avenue and fired at him, missing and striking William Murphy of 113 West Sixtieth street, a passer-by, in the arm.

Hearing the shot, Gerhard saw Bland run into the street with a revolver, where a trolley car knocked him down and "nearly killed" him, and a small boy made off with the dropped weapon. Bleeding from cuts on the head, Bland ran through Sixty-fourth street to West End avenue, where Gerhard found him in a saloon.

By the time Gerhard and three other policemen set out for the station with their prisoner, the Sun reported, "a crowd of a thousand had collected." The crowd gave the officers "plenty of trouble" on the way to Sixty-eighth street, and according to Gerhard many stones struck both Bland and the policemen. Neither paper describes injuries from the stones or any arrests among the crowd.

On August 2 Bland was arraigned in the West Side court on a charge of shooting Murphy, and Magistrate Pool held him in $1,000 bail for examination on Tuesday. No report of the examination's outcome was found.

Two New York dailies covered the court hearing on August 3, and they differed in what they chose to report. The Sun headlined its story "CROWD STONES NEGRO PRISONER," called Bland "a big negro longshoreman," and noted that the wounded Murphy had been "taking the highball treatment" in a saloon. The New-York Tribune, under "HELD FOR SHOOTING WRONG MAN," described Bland as "a colored man" from Brooklyn and said nothing of a crowd or stones. No Black-press coverage of the episode was found.

reader.title: Stoning of Preston Bland
bases: A crowd that the Sun put at a thousand threw stones at a Black prisoner being taken to the station by four policemen; no one was killed and no intent to kill is reported (A1).

The shooting, arrest and bail are reported by two papers (A1, A2), but the crowd and the stoning appear only in the Sun, on the word of one policeman (A1); the Tribune neither confirms nor denies it (A2).

accounts.label: Policeman Gerhard (in court, per the Sun)
accounts.gist: A crowd of a thousand collected as four policemen took Bland to the station, and many stones hit Bland and the officers.

accounts.label: Policeman Gerhard (in court, per the Tribune)
accounts.gist: Bland quarrelled with another Black man, fired, missed and hit Murphy, then was knocked down by a trolley car while running from Gerhard; no crowd is mentioned.

framing.detail: The Sun headlined "CROWD STONES NEGRO PRISONER", called Bland "a big negro longshoreman" and "the negro", and noted the wounded Murphy's "highball treatment"; it reported the stoning without comment.
The Tribune headlined "HELD FOR SHOOTING WRONG MAN", called Bland "a colored man", and reported only the shooting charge.
